# Documentation review: report-builder

**Scope:** `README.md` is the only project documentation. I left out the files under `.claude/skills/` because they configure the agent tooling and aren't documentation for this project. I checked what the README says against `package.json` and `src/main.js`.

**Audience (my inference):** developers who want to run the report builder locally. The evidence is that the README has only a requirements section and a build section, and `package.json` defines `start` and `test` scripts. Correct me if the readers are someone else, such as analysts who only use the reports.

## Classification

| Page | Intended form | Actual form | Need it serves |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `README.md` | Landing page plus quick start (how-to) | A short how-to with a one-line summary | "Get the report builder running" |

The form suits the need. The problems are that the facts are wrong and some content is missing, not the page type.

## Findings

| Severity | Location | Evidence | Suggested fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| blocker | `README.md:11` | The README says to run `npm run build`, but `package.json:7-10` defines only `start` and `test`. Following the README as written stops at the first command with npm's "Missing script" error, so the reader never reaches `npm start`. | Remove the build step. If a build is planned, add the script first. |
| blocker | `README.md:7` | The README says "Node.js 18 or later", but `package.json:5` declares `"node": ">=22"`. Readers on Node 18 or 20 will install a version the project doesn't support. | Change it to "Node.js 22 or later". `engines` is the source of truth, so point to it or keep the two in sync. |
| major | `README.md:3` | "Builds weekly usage reports from the events table" doesn't say which database or table, how to connect, what credentials or environment variables are needed, or where the report ends up. `src/main.js:1` only prints `report`, so the code doesn't back up the claim either. | Add a short section on configuration and output: the data source, connection settings, and where the output goes and in what format. If the feature isn't built yet, say so. |
| minor | `README.md:9-11` | The heading "Build" covers running the tool, and the steps sit in a sentence instead of a numbered list or a copyable code block. | Rename it to "Run the report builder" and use numbered steps with a `sh` code block. |
| minor | `README.md` (missing section) | `package.json:9` defines `npm test`, but the README never mentions tests. | Add a "Run the tests" section with `npm test`. |
| minor | `README.md` (missing section) | The README names no owner, maintainer, or support contact, and the repo has no `CODEOWNERS` file. | Add a maintainer or support line. I couldn't find evidence of who the owner is, so the user needs to supply it. |
| nit | `README.md:1` | The title "Report builder" doesn't match the package name `report-builder` (`package.json:2`) and gives no version. Version 2.1.0 has no changelog or release reference. | Consider using `report-builder` in the title and linking to a changelog if one exists. |

## Strengths

- The page is short and starts with a one-line statement of what the tool does, so it passes the three-second test.
- It lists prerequisites before the steps.
- It has a single H1, no skipped heading levels, and sentence-case headings. Without images, tables or links, there are no accessibility problems in what exists.

## Suggested diffs

```diff
 ## Requirements

-- Node.js 18 or later
+- Node.js 22 or later (see `engines` in `package.json`)

-## Build
+## Run the report builder

-Run `npm run build`, then `npm start`.
+```sh
+npm start
+```
+
+## Run the tests
+
+```sh
+npm test
+```
```

## Unevaluated

This session didn't allow running commands or writing files, so I couldn't check the following:

- **Commands:** I didn't run `npm run build`, `npm start` or `npm test`. The blocker on `README.md:11` comes from reading `package.json`, not from running the command.
- **Linters:** the project doesn't configure markdownlint, Vale or a link checker, and I couldn't run any of them anyway.
- **Freshness and ownership history:** the directory isn't a git repository, so I couldn't check last-modified dates or past authors.
- **Report check:** I couldn't save this report and run the skill's `scripts/check-review-report.mjs` on it.
